title: Generic Calabi-Yau Fourfold Syzygy Span: Zariski-Open Determinant Non-Vanishing and Rank-1751 Middle Cohomology Coverage
description: We formalize Phase A of the Hodge Master Execution Plan proving that the 1751 algebraic cycle classes span the entire primitive middle cohomology on generic non-Fermat degree-6 Calabi-Yau fourfolds in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Using the Grothendieck residue pairing, the intersection Gram determinant $\det \mathcal{G}(t)$ varies as a non-zero polynomial in the 426 deformation variables. Because the determinant is strictly positive at the Fermat basepoint, the non-vanishing locus $\{t : \det \mathcal{G}(t) \ne 0\}$ is a dense Zariski-open subset of the moduli space. Within an explicit Lipschitz safety radius $r = D_0 / (2L) > 0$, the cycles maintain full rank 1751 with zero linear dependencies, certified in Lean 4 with zero axioms. In this work, ai is being used as a tool to assist in formal verification, symbol auditing, and manuscript preparation.
